title: Pests have no idle animation, only plants do
description: The second half of James's 'animate all the plants and enemies' ask. Plant._wobble_time now drives an idle sway for every placed plant (plant-tower-defense-04x), but Pest has no equivalent - a walking aphid or beetle is a static sprite sliding along the road, and the new facing rotation (129) made that more visible, not less. Give pests idle/locomotion motion (a walk bob, antenna twitch, wing flutter for winged mutations), gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled() and cheap enough for SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING pests at once.

title: An animated dandelion that blows its seeds as bombs, in an epic packet tier
description: James's direct ask, still unshipped. A fifth plant: seed-puff attack animation where the dandelion visibly loses fluff as it fires, and seeds that ARC and DETONATE rather than travelling straight like a Corn Cobbler kernel or landing instantly like a Chomp bite. Ships in a new 'epic' seed packet tier above the current common/rare split (see SeedBank.PACKET_COST / packet_pool and PlantCatalog). Needs art in art_src/ per STYLE.md (64x64, top-down, up-screen facing, outline = darker shade of fill) rasterised to assets/sprites/ + retina, and must pass test_sprite_style.gd's contract.

title: More waves, and a boss pest
description: James's direct ask, still unshipped. WaveDirector.WAVES ends at 8 fixed waves before endless takes over with escalating mutation chance on the same two pests (aphid, beetle). Add real additional waves to the table, and at least one boss pest: bigger health pool, a distinct sprite, and a mechanic that is NOT just 'armoured but more'. Note the endless scaling (health_scale_for/speed_scale_for/mutation_chance_for) and SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING budget already exist and are tested - extending the table must keep those honest.

title: Four tests write the developer's real user://highscore.save
description: test_selftest.gd:679 (test_run_config_high_score_only_ever_goes_up), :1014, :4326 and :4921 (test_a_record_set_by_quitting_is_announced_on_the_title_screen) all set RunConfig.campaign_high_score/endless_high_score in memory and then call RunConfig.record_score(), while RunConfig.save_path is still the REAL user://highscore.save. record_score() calls _save(), so each headless suite run rewrites the developer's own save with whatever number the test just staged. Observed over two runs of the full suite on 2026-08-16: the file went v5/308/5008 -> v6/310/5010 -> v6/2/2. Both high scores were destroyed; only a scratchpad copy taken before the work brought them back. These tests stash and restore the in-memory scores, which is what makes it invisible -- the FILE keeps the last number written. Fix: give each of them the scratch-save redirect test_economy._with_scratch_save already implements (RunConfig.save_path = a user://test_*.save, restore and delete afterwards), or add the same wrapper to test_selftest.gd. Related: harness issue #33 (--isolated isolates the bus, not user://), which makes this worse under two concurrent agents.
close_reason: Fixed: four tests redirected to scratch paths (three named in the bead plus a fourth in test_economy.gd found by the new guard), scores restored as well as save_path, and test_no_test_persists_through_the_players_own_save added as a comment-stripping source guard. Real save verified byte-identical across two full suite runs.

title: Sweep test/ for other group reads taken by index
description: test_kernels_launch read kernels[0] from a tree-global group and measured a leaked object every run - green for months, red the moment four unrelated tests were appended. Nothing enumerates the other group reads (pests, husks, kernels, plants); any taken by index has the same defect. A sweep for get_nodes_in_group(...)[0] in test/ finds the rest in one pass.

title: A damaged plant's health bar eats clicks on the playfield
description: Plant._health_back and _health_bar are ColorRects with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, parked over the playfield. A damaged plant therefore has a 32x5 strip that swallows clicks meant for the board. Pre-existing; found while adding the health bar notches.

title: Post-mortem calls your best chokepoint your weakest ground
description: Game._note_lane_loss is called from _on_pest_died (every kill, at the pest's position) as well as _on_pest_escaped. So _run_losses counts kills, not damage. That is correct for LanePressureOverlay, whose doc says 'how far did pests get' - a kill at cell 30 of 40 IS pressure. But run_summary.gd:201 _worst_cell_text() labels the highest-count cell 'Weakest ground - N lost there', so a well-defended chokepoint is reported to the player as their weakest ground, every run. The advice is not just useless, it is inverted. Found by the agent building the prep depth readout, which declined to reuse worst_run_cell() for exactly this reason.

title: A truncated save silently zeroes a high score that can never be restored
description: RunConfig._save stamps a SAVE_VERSION line on every write and _load tests only begins_with('v') -- the version is written and never actually read, so a future format change has no migration hook despite the field existing to provide one. Worse, int('') is 0 in GDScript, so a truncated or partially-written save loads as a zero high score, and record_score only ever raises a record: once it reads 0 the real number is gone forever with no way back. A save file is the one thing in this project the player cannot regenerate by playing.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed, truncated or short save leaves the existing in-memory scores untouched rather than zeroing them, and the version field is actually consulted. Unit tests cover a truncated file, a garbage file, and a future version number.

title: Quitting an endless run through pause files no score
description: RunConfig.record_score has exactly one caller, Game._end_run, reached only from the victory branch or from lives hitting 0. has_more_waves() is unconditionally true in endless, so victory is unreachable there -- meaning the ONLY way to bank an endless score is to lose. Cycle 8's pause screen then added two exits that bypass _end_run entirely: RestartButton calls reload_current_scene and GateButton calls change_scene_to_file. So a player who quits a long endless run voluntarily files nothing, and the run they were most likely to be proud of is the one guaranteed not to count.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving a run through any exit files the score exactly once, and a re-entry cannot file it twice. Unit test covers quitting via both pause exits.

title: Uproot-as-score: refunds credit seeds_earned_total, so plant-uproot cycling inflates the high score
description: SeedBank.refund routes through add_seeds, which increments seeds_earned_total -- the number both per-mode high scores are kept on. So planting a Corn for 10 and uprooting it for 6 costs 4 seeds of wallet and CREDITS 6 to the recorded score, repeatably. A 100-seed float converts to roughly +150 score with no gameplay at all. Scaling the refund by health in cycle 7 killed uproot-as-repair and left this untouched; the seed_bank comment 'Refunds count too' documents the behaviour as deliberate, but it predates high scores being a scoreboard players compete on.
acceptance_criteria: Uprooting cannot raise seeds_earned_total. A unit test plants and uproots in a loop and asserts the recorded score does not move, while ordinary income still counts.

title: Common seed packets silently become rare ones once Chomp unlocks
description: SeedBank._roll_packet filters the locked pool to ids at or below the packet's max_tier, then falls back to the WHOLE locked pool when that filtered pool is empty. Chomp is tier 1 and Sunflower is tier 2, so the moment Chomp unlocks the filtered pool for a common packet is always empty and a 20-seed common packet can hand out the tier-2 Sunflower. That makes the two packet tiers indistinguishable in the only way they were supposed to differ, and both tooltips become false: the common button says 'tier 1 only' and the rare one says 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'.
acceptance_criteria: A common packet can never yield a plant above its max_tier. When nothing at or below that tier remains locked, the purchase is refused with a reason rather than silently upgraded, and the tooltips match the behaviour. Unit test covers the exhausted-pool case.
close_reason: Common packets refuse rather than falling back to the whole locked pool; no charge on refusal, no soft-lock possible. Fixed a pre-existing test that was green only because of the bug.

title: Style contract + first sprite set (Corn Cobbler, Chomp Flower, pests, seed packet)
description: Measured the Kenney Tower Defense kit's conventions into art_src/STYLE.md, authored 6 SVG sources, rasterised them to assets/sprites (64) + retina (128), and gated the contract with test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd.

title: [bug] A budgets test picks a node out of a tree-global group by first-match
description: test/unit/test_placement.gd:3035 test_the_budgets_verb_degrades_per_entry_with_no_game_in_the_tree() calls get_first_node_in_group('game') - 'whichever one the engine lists first' by definition, with no index to drop. Flagged by group_leak_check.py on at least three separate agent runs across this session and never fixed. Diff the group around the action instead, or hold the node the test itself created. See the godot-test-isolation skill, which is about exactly this failure mode.

title: Eight public functions from the overlay refactor and title grid have no test naming them
description: suite_reach_check reports 8 NEW findings: game/overlay_screen.gd add_heading/add_note_label/add_row_label/add_row_button/add_back_button/footer_y, and game/title_screen.gd menu_rows/row_height. These are the public builder surface the OverlayScreen extraction (q7b) and the title menu grid (w5k) introduced. The agent that surfaced them deliberately did NOT run --baseline-write, which would have banked them as accepted debt. Write real tests that exercise each - naming a symbol in an assert message does not count as reach, and suite_reach_check is namespace-blind so a same-named getter elsewhere can credit the wrong one.

title: Three overlays build the same chrome three times
description: key_binding_screen.gd (347 lines), options_screen.gd (350) and notebook_screen.gd (758) each hand-roll a Backdrop ColorRect at Color(GardenTheme.INK, 0.88), a Paper Panel via paper_panel(), a BackButton top-left, and a back_requested signal. Options was written by copying Keys deliberately, hence identical node names. The shared layout rule - panel sized from row count, footer clearance is a minimum GAP not mere non-intersection because Rect2.intersects is false for boxes sharing an edge - is stated twice and enforced by two separate tests. Extract an OverlayScreen base owning backdrop/paper/BackButton/back_requested plus that one assertion, leaving each screen only its own rows. Keep the documented node-path contracts intact (the bridge and test_selftest.gd press them by name).

title: Persist the two mute flags in the save beside colorblind_safe
description: Sfx._muted and Music._muted are static and die with the process; RunConfig.compose_save writes one options line (cb0/cb1) and nothing for either mute. The Options screen (plant-tower-defense-lgv) reads and writes all three, so two of its three rows silently reset on every launch while the third does not. Fix means extending the save format: it is at v5, and v3/v4 are BOTH refused on sight because two branches minted their own v3 in parallel -- so bump deliberately to v6, migrate forward from v5 (a v5 file has no mute fields; both default to unmuted, exactly as v2 -> v5 handles its three added fields), keep compose_save the single writer shape, and add round-trip tests plus a v5-file-reads-forward test.

title: The longest pause-card legend row draws past the paper
description: PauseScreen._build_key_list assigns each KeyRow Label a width of card_rect().size.x - 56 (264) at x = CARD_X + 28 (316). node-bounds on the live game reports KeyRow4 as 316, 553, 326x26 -- the Label's own minimum size wins over the assigned 264, so the longest row ('C   colourblind-safe health and threat bars') draws ~34px past the card's right edge at 608, onto the dimmed backdrop over the live board. Pre-existing: nothing about the row's x or width changed in plant-tower-defense-ac0, which is where it was spotted. Nothing gates it -- the existing pause-card layout test asserts only the vertical fit and pairwise overlap, and clip_text makes get_minimum_size() useless for the obvious width assertion (use _T.text_width). Fix is either a shorter 'does' phrase for that verb, a smaller font for the legend, or setting clip_text's minimum properly; whichever, assert the drawn width against the paper the way NotebookScreen.SUBHEAD_MAX_WIDTH is asserted.

title: Every persisted option is reachable by one keystroke and no menu
description: garden_colorblind, garden_mute_sfx and garden_mute_music all persist through RunConfig, and the only surface any has is a keystroke plus a HUD sentence. The Keys screen can rebind those keys but cannot set the options they toggle - so the screen that exists for configuration is the one place a player cannot see whether the colourblind bars are currently on. Add an Options surface (a second column on the Keys screen, or a sibling screen) reading/writing the three flags that already round-trip.

title: An earned milestone is announced once and then has nowhere to live
description: RunSummary.new_milestones() (run_summary.gd:424) reads only ids the run JUST earned and MilestoneRibbon draws only those, so a milestone earned three runs ago is saved in RunConfig.earned_milestones and never visible again. The set is persisted and has_milestone() is public but called by nothing outside the save's own tests. Add a trophy shelf on the title screen or a notebook page listing all milestones with earned/unearned state.

title: The Keys screen is unreachable from inside a run
description: KeysButton is built in TitleScreen (title_screen.gd:262, opening KeyBindingScreen at :469); pause_screen.gd never mentions KeyBindingScreen. The player who most wants to move a key - the one who just pressed the wrong one mid-run - must abandon the run to reach it. Same shape as the cycle-11 notebook gap, fixed then by a fourth pause-card button; the card has since grown a fifth and PauseScreen.card_rect() derives height from contents, so check whether it still fits and decide what gives rather than blindly adding a sixth.

title: A Sunflower's payout has no sound and no visual glyph
description: Game._on_plant_grew_seeds (game.gd:1013-1014), the handler for every Sunflower payout, is one bare line: bank.add_seeds(amount). Contrast Game._on_husk_collected, which now plays Sfx.HUSK_COLLECTED and calls hud.fly_seed_glyph() (this cycle's o2b). Give the Sunflower's payout the same two channels: a sound (check Sfx.SOUNDS for a reusable coin/chime entry first) and a fly_seed_glyph() call from the plant's own board position.
close_reason: Shipped in 6dbbe19: Game._on_plant_grew_seeds now plays Sfx.SEEDS_GROWN (HUSK_COLLECTED's handleCoins.ogg, trimmed -7 dB with a 200ms repeat gate) and calls hud.fly_seed_glyph from the paying plant's own board position. The plant is bound at the connect site in place_plant, so Sunflower.grew_seeds still emits only an amount. Verified live: FxLayer held one glyph on the line from the flower's global (32,104) to the Seeds label, and Voice0 loaded handleCoins.ogg at volume_db -7.0.

title: Pest.flash_hit() exists and only Kernel ever calls it
description: The hit cue added for plant-tower-defense-7o3 (Pest.flash_hit(), pest.gd:531) is called only from kernel.gd:76. ChompFlower's bite and StickySundew's claim land real damage/kills with no visual tell at all - a ranged kernel now marks its hit and a melee plant's is exactly as invisible as before. Call flash_hit() (or a variant) from ChompFlower._bite() and StickySundew._claim() at the moment damage actually lands.
close_reason: ChompFlower._bite() and StickySundew._claim() now call pest.flash_hit() at the moment of catch, guarded by is_alive() like the kernel site

title: A refused plant upgrade has no denial cue, unlike plant/packet purchases
description: Hud.shake_plant_button()/shake_packet_button() plus Sfx.PURCHASE_DENIED (game.gd:1128, 1303) fire on a refused plant placement or packet buy, but Game.upgrade_selected() (game.gd:1012-1026) still answers an underfunded upgrade with only hud.show_message() - the exact gap 8kx closed everywhere else. Add the same shake+sound treatment to the Upgrade button.
close_reason: Added Hud.shake_upgrade_button() and Sfx.PURCHASE_DENIED to Game.upgrade_selected()'s underfunded path, plus a unit test; verified live with slowed game speed that the button rotates mid-shake

title: A kernel hit and a kernel miss both just vanish
description: Kernel._physics_process (kernel.gd:60-72) has exactly two exits: leave _bounds and queue_free(), or land inside HIT_RADIUS of a pest, call take_damage(), and queue_free() - same call, same frame, no visual distinction between the two. Every plant now has its own attack cue (y62) and every pest death fades (3t9); the projectile connecting them has no impact flash, spark, or differently-timed vanish to say a hit landed. Add a brief impact cue (a small flash/particle burst or a one-frame flicker on the pest hit) distinct from a kernel simply leaving the board.
close_reason: Kernel connects now flash the surviving pest (Pest.flash_hit / hit_flash_color), gated by GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); a lethal hit still relies on the existing corpse/fade/PEST_KILLED cue. Verified headless (name_check, import, lint, run_tests 420/420) and live via devtools bridge (step-time caught modulate mid-flash at 1.43, boosted above 1.0).

title: None of the three attacking plants calls Sfx.play() for its own attack
description: CornCobbler._fire_at() (corn_cobbler.gd:116-132) spawns kernels and calls _recoil() with no sound; ChompFlower._grab()/_bite() (chomp_flower.gd:77-84,139-144) closes the mouth with no sound; StickySundew._claim() (sticky_sundew.gd:244-250) has the same gap. Every combat sound today is centralised in game.gd and fires on the pest's reaction (Sfx.PEST_KILLED, Sfx.PLANT_BITTEN) rather than the attacker's own action, so a Corn Cobbler volleying five kernels or a Chomp snapping shut are silent on the attacker's end. Add a distinct Sfx entry per plant's own attack verb, played from the plant itself at the moment it acts.
close_reason: Added CORN_FIRED, CHOMP_BITE, SUNDEW_CLAIM to Sfx, each reusing an existing vendored stream; wired into CornCobbler._fire_at, ChompFlower._bite, StickySundew._claim. Commit a2f91d9.

title: Plant idle sway is a dead field
description: Plant._wobble_time (plant.gd:104) is declared and never read or written anywhere else in the file - a sweep of every var declared in game/ found exactly one field with no second reference. Wire it up: a small sin(_wobble_time * k) sway on _sprite.rotation (or similar idle motion), gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), incremented in _physics_process. Ties to James's direct ask ('animate all the plants and enemies') - this is the hook already sitting there for exactly that, unwired. Scope to Plant only for this issue; pests can follow separately.
close_reason: Wired _wobble_time into _physics_process; small sin() sway on the sprite, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), phased per-cell. Commit 5792e57.

title: Clearing a wave gets a single status-row sentence, starting one gets a banner and a sound
description:
Game._check_wave_cleared() (game.gd:322-338) sets _wave_live = false, commits the
lane pressure map, and calls hud.show_message(Hud.wave_cleared_line(...), 6.0) -- no
Sfx.play(), no flash, nothing on the board itself. _on_wave_started plays
Sfx.WAVE_STARTED (game.gd:272) into a 48px banner the instant a wave begins
(Hud.announce_wave, hud.gd:1044-1053). The wave a player survives currently
announces itself more quietly than the wave about to attack them. Give clearing a
wave its own cue -- a Sfx entry and/or a brief board-level flourish -- proportionate
to what it is.
close_reason: Added Sfx.WAVE_CLEARED and Hud.announce_wave_cleared, sharing the banner mechanism via _show_banner; wired into _check_wave_cleared alongside the existing status line. Commit 075fce9.

title: RunSummary's entrance does not know whether the run was won or lost
description:
_build_heading() (run_summary.gd:144-153) picks a different heading text and colour
for victory ("The garden holds!" vs "The garden is eaten"), but _play_entrance()
(run_summary.gd:462-470) rises every Control by the identical RISE_OFFSET over the
identical RISE_SECONDS with no branch on `won` anywhere in it. Give a win and a loss
distinct entrance motion (or a distinct one-shot flourish, e.g. a brief flash/shake
on loss) so the card's motion agrees with what its heading already says.
close_reason: Entrance branches on won: faster/overshoot rise for a win, slower plain rise for a loss. Commit 9e06db2.

title: A pest corpse pops out of existence instead of fading
description:
_play_death() (pest.gd:484-505) swaps to the dead-eyes texture, holds it for
DEATH_LINGER (0.35s, pest.gd:136), then tween.tween_callback(queue_free) -- nothing
tweens modulate.a first, so the corpse is at full opacity on its last frame and
simply gone the next. Every other exit in this game fades: Plant.play_exit_and_free()
shrinks a sprite to zero before freeing, and a pest's own arrival fades it in. Add a
short fade-out (gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled()) into the existing
tween chain before queue_free.
close_reason: modulate:a now tweens to 0 over the tail of DEATH_LINGER, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); commit ab3d8f3

title: Pests never turn to face the direction they're walking
description:
Requested directly by James (kanban.md, 'Requested directly by James' block). Pest
sprites are drawn up-screen per the art style convention, but pest.gd has no
rotation/flip_h/flip_v logic anywhere -- a pest walking down, left, or right the road
still renders facing up-screen the whole way. Give Pest a facing update (rotation or
flip, whichever the kit's sprites tolerate) driven off its walk direction each leg of
PATH_CORNERS.
close_reason: Sprite rotates to face the leg it is walking, snapped to 4 cardinal directions off Board's axis-aligned route; commit 3815587

title: A plant leaving the board always vanishes silently
description: Both Game._on_plant_destroyed (game.gd:987-995) and Game.uproot_selected (game.gd:1084-1093) end in plant.queue_free() with no exit animation; uproot additionally has zero Sfx.play() call anywhere in the function. Neither tweens the sprite out the way Plant._build_visuals tweens one in (plant.gd:187-190, 0.4x to 1.12x to 1.0 over 0.22s). A create_tween() shrinking _sprite.scale toward zero before either queue_free() call, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), plus an Sfx entry for uproot specifically, would give leaving the board the same care arriving on it gets.

title: Corn Cobbler upgrades have no moment of their own
description: CornCobbler.upgrade() (corn_cobbler.gd:290-297) bumps level and calls queue_redraw() -- a static fact the muzzle fan picks up next paint, not a cue at the instant the player spends the seeds. Contrast ChompFlower._bite() (chomp_flower.gd:139-144), which squashes its sprite on every single meal. A short scale-pop on the cob's sprite plus a new Sfx entry, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), would mark the transaction rather than only its aftermath.

title: A refused purchase has a sentence and no other feedback
description: SeedBank.pay_for_plant() and buy_packet() both emit purchase_failed with only a reason string on every refusal (seed_bank.gd:111-121, 179-190), and Game._ready wires it straight to hud.show_message(reason) - a caption in the shared status line, nothing more. Sfx.SOUNDS has entries for planting, a plant dying, a pest dying, a wave starting, but none for a purchase bouncing. Add a denial cue: a short red shake on the button actually clicked (or the plant bar slot) plus a new Sfx.SOUNDS entry, so the 'no' lands where the click happened instead of only in text a player mid-wave may not be reading.
close_reason: Shipped: Sfx.PURCHASE_DENIED (reuses error_002.ogg) plays on every bank.purchase_failed; Hud.shake_plant_button/shake_packet_button shake the specific control at the two call sites that know which one was reached for. Commit 2a162f3.

title: Selecting a plant has no motion
description: Plant.set_selected() (plant.gd:462-468) toggles _selection_marker.visible directly and SelectionMarker._draw_brackets() (selection_marker.gd:41-46) draws the four corner brackets at fixed size the instant the flag flips - no tween, nothing between invisible and full-size. Contrast _build_visuals(), which pops a placed plant's sprite in from 0.4x scale over 0.22s (plant.gd:187-190). Give the selection brackets (and by inheritance PlacementPreview's hover cue) a short grow-in/fade tween instead of an instant show, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled().
close_reason: Shipped: SelectionMarker.play_entrance() grows brackets in from 0.55x/transparent. PlacementPreview stays instant (hover cue, redraws every mouse move) -- documented in the commit. Commit 506a0f9.

title: HUD readouts snap instead of punching on change
description: Hud.refresh() overwrites _seeds_label.text, _lives_label.text and _compost_label.text outright every call (hud.gd:731,753,755), while the same file already eases the wave label's colour with a killed-and-restarted Tween in _ease_threat_tint (hud.gd:898-911) instead of snapping it. Give the seeds/lives/compost labels a short scale-punch when their value changes, gated the same way _ease_threat_tint already is (GardenTheme.animations_enabled()), so the game's three most frequent feedback moments (a kill payout, a life lost, a husk composted) get the one motion vocabulary this file has already proven out.
close_reason: Shipped: seeds/lives/compost labels get a scale punch on change, reusing _ease_threat_tint's kill-and-restart Tween pattern. Commit 7296b78.

title: PauseScreen has no entrance or exit motion
description: PauseScreen's own header calls it shaped after RunSummary, being the same kind of object: a card over a live board (pause_screen.gd:12-14). RunSummary and TitleScreen both rise their content in against GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); PauseScreen has no create_tween or modulate write anywhere in the file. The card appears via add_child and disappears via _pause_layer.queue_free() (game.gd:821) on the same frame Escape is pressed. Add a rise-in / fade-out matching the other two card screens' pattern, gated the same way.
close_reason: Shipped: rise-in entrance borrowing RunSummary's constants, and a play_exit() fade Game.resume_run() awaits before freeing the layer. Commit 54152de.

title: Corn Cobbler needs a readiness readout
description: Sunflower's payout clock has an always-on fill gauge (sunflower.gd ~150-156) and Chomp Flower's mouth shows a shrinking chew ring (chomp_flower.gd _draw ~130-136), but CornCobbler._cooldown (corn_cobbler.gd:88, ticked at ~95-97) is read by nothing outside _act(). The muzzle fan (_draw_muzzle_fan, ~141-152) reflects the last shot's spread, not the next shot's timing, so a cob mid-reload and one ready to fire look identical. Add a readiness cue (fill ring, dimming muzzle, or similar) driven off _cooldown / LEVELS interval, matching the visual idiom the other two plants already use.
close_reason: Readiness fade shipped: readiness_at()/readiness() drive a 0.35-1.0 alpha fade on the muzzle fan, off the same _cooldown _act already ticks. Unit-tested exactly (pure math + wired through real _act()); live-confirmed via forced fires (0.02-0.10 readiness right after firing, 1.0 once recovered), zero runtime errors across 7 placed cobblers. Baseline regenerated (fire_interval() is now genuinely test-named). Commit follows.

title: Find tests that read state straight after instantiate_scene
description: test_hosting_a_loaded_cob asserted a volley had fired by the time instantiate_scene returned. That frame count is unspecified, so it was order-dependent - green two cycles, red when unrelated tests shifted timing. Any test reading a group or a live property straight after instantiate_scene without awaiting a condition has the same exposure. A checker for that shape would name them.

title: Tell the player unaimed ground still gets kills
description: Coverage is now measured both directions and neither number is in the game. Under-promise: 7 kills on unaimed ground at up to 202px, because a kernel flies until it leaves the board. Over-promise at the pest: zero of 116. The board says 'unaimed', which is right, but a player never learns unaimed ground still gets kills - which is what would stop them over-buying cover.

title: Assert what Pest.died and escaped carry
description: 15 signals still have nothing asserting what they carry, down from 17. Pest.died is the highest value remaining: it is the income path with the most wiring under it (Game._on_pest_died drops the husk, banks seeds, notes the lane loss). escaped is its pair. Assert the payload and which paths fire, not merely that the signal exists - naming it satisfies the reach gate while proving nothing.

title: No gate says how much of the game the suite never touches
description: run_tests prints Suite: 7 scripts and Assertions: N; the checkers print N of M; lint prints Shaders: N of M. Nothing prints which .gd files are never loaded by any test. The bridge already has scripts-seen and nothing compares it against the file list. That is the one denominator the project lacks, and it is the one that says where the suite is blind.

title: Tell the player which red means fought and which means unreachable
description: coverage_frontier() says how far the garden can reach; LanePressureOverlay says how far pests got. The prep line compares them once to pick a sentence. The board never does - a player sees red tint and cannot tell 'they got here and we fought' from 'they got here and nothing could touch them', which is the whole distinction the coverage work established.

title: Warn at startup when a budget crosses its own tight threshold
description: cmd budgets reports tight/spent from outside, but nothing inside the game reacts. A startup push_warning when any budget crosses its tight threshold means the next person to spend one hears about it on the next run rather than on the next audit. Reuses the budget entries the verb already computes.

title: Tests leak nodes into groups and nothing notices
description: Root cause under the kernels flake: a test that builds a Kernel and does not free it leaves it in the group for every later test. _T.free_ui is called on hosts, but a kernel spawned by _act is parented to the host's PARENT, not the host. A per-test assertion that group counts return to where they started would catch the whole class.

title: Two HUD budgets sit within 8px of their ceilings
description: cmd budgets reports hud_readouts at 161 of 168px (SeedsLabel, 7px left) and hud_stats_row at 1104 of 1112px (8px left). Both are 'tight' by the verb's own <15% threshold. The row sum is the one that matters: widening any single readout is paid out of it, so the two are coupled and both are nearly gone. Worth deciding now whether the stats row needs re-proportioning before the next readout is added rather than after.
close_reason: Shipped: trimmed STATS_SEPARATION 14->10, flat +10px readout margins, ratcheted BUDGET_FLOOR, commit e93241c

title: SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING is fully spent and nothing said so
description: cmd budgets reports pest_road_ceiling at 40 of 40 pests, 0 left, state 'spent'. That is by construction - the ceiling is enforced by the group shares summing to it exactly - but it means the road budget has no slack at all, so any future wave shape that wants more simultaneous pests has nowhere to take them from. Decide whether 'spent by design' deserves its own state distinct from 'spent because you ran out'.
close_reason: Shipped: Game.BUDGET_SPENT_BY_DESIGN state, pest_road_ceiling passes by_design=true, commit 34a77ae

title: The post-mortem names a cell the road under it may not be reddest at
description: stop_cell is losses-minus-escapes; the tint under the translucent summary card is still painted from raw losses. On a bleeding run the named cell and the reddest cell genuinely differ. Correct and documented, but a player looking from the number to the picture is told nothing. Either the card points at its own cell, or the tint switches to stops.

title: A budgets verb that prints every declared coupling with its headroom
description: Four constants now carry 'moving me costs you X' comments: PATH_CORNERS, COLLECT_RADIUS, SUBHEAD_MAX_WIDTH and the HUD WORST_CASE_TEXT budgets. Each warns about a coupling living in another file, and a person only finds the warning by editing that exact line. A devtools verb printing every declared budget with its current headroom makes the set visible before someone goes looking.

title: Name the husk budget where the road is actually edited
description: board_info now reports the husk click budget, but reaching it needs a running game, a launched bridge and knowing the verb exists. A designer dragging Board.PATH_CORNERS is in board.gd in an editor and nothing there mentions the budget. Add a ## line above PATH_CORNERS and above CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS naming it. Suggested by the agent that built the devtools half, which correctly judged its own work a half-solution.

title: Give the board a second warning channel so red is not carrying three meanings
description: GardenTheme.DANGER now paints lane pressure (pests got this far), the plant health bar (this plant is dying) and an armed Uproot (you are about to destroy this). Three different sentences in one hue at three alphas. Unifying the value was right; colour alone should not carry three meanings - add a shape or hatch channel.

title: Put husk_click_margin in board_info so the budget is visible before a test fails
description: husk_click_margin() exists because the husk-vs-placement conflict is 4px from being real, and a test asserts the clearance stays positive. Nothing tells a designer moving PATH_CORNERS or COLLECT_RADIUS that they are spending it - they find out when a test fails, with no indication 4px was the budget.

title: Show lane pressure during prep, not after the run
description: LanePressureOverlay paints how far pests got, decayed once per wave, and is a readout of the wave that just ended. Board.run_pressure_alpha exists and is shown exactly once by show_run_pressure(), at the moment the run is over. The number that would inform a purchase is held back until purchasing has stopped. Surface it during the prep strip.

title: The notebook is unreachable the moment a run starts
description: NotebookScreen is constructed in exactly one place, title_screen.gd's _open_notebook(), and nothing in game.gd, hud.gd or pause_screen.gd can reach it. So the game's only explanation of anything is closed to the player who actually needs it -- mid-run, holding a plant they do not understand. The pause card is now a full-screen surface that already lists the keyboard verbs and is already the only way to leave a run; a fourth button on it is the whole fix. NotebookScreen already emits back_requested and is built to be added as a child of any Control.
acceptance_criteria: The notebook opens from within a run and returns to the paused game, with the run still paused behind it. A test asserts the pause state survives opening and closing it.

title: The endless spawn gap floors at wave 22 and only the count keeps climbing
description: WaveDirector's aphid spawn gap reaches its floor around wave 22, and the health and speed scales cap around waves 41 and 48. Past 48 the only thing that still moves is count, which is uncapped -- 166 pests at wave 48, 376 at wave 108. Spawn floor times crossing time puts on the order of 100 aphids alive at once on an 896px board. That is precisely the quantity problem the ENDLESS_HEALTH_STEP header says the scales exist to avoid, arrived at from the other direction.
acceptance_criteria: Endless difficulty past the scale caps escalates by something other than raw count, or count is bounded and the difficulty comes from elsewhere. A test asserts simultaneous pest count stays under a stated ceiling at wave 100.

title: A husk eats the click that would have planted, and the preview cannot warn about it
description: CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS is 28, so a husk claims a 56px-wide target on a 64px cell -- 88% of it. Game._click_at sweeps a husk before it reaches the placement branch and returns, so a click on a cell the preview has just drawn as legal composts instead of planting. PlacementPreview now computes four states (illegal, at_risk, dead ground, redundant coverage) and mentions husks exactly zero times, so the one thing that can silently take the click is the one thing the ring cannot warn about. Husks last up to 10s, so the cell is effectively unplantable for that long with no indication.
acceptance_criteria: Either the preview shows that a click on this cell will compost rather than plant, or placement wins on a cell the player has explicitly targeted. Unit test covers a husk overlapping a buildable cell.
close_reason: Precedence fixed: a click that would plant, plants. Measurement showed the conflict cannot occur on the shipping board (32px vs a 28px sweep, 4px margin) -- husk_click_margin() now gates that

title: Every Sundew redraw walks every pest on the board
description: StickySundew._draw_wash calls shared_ground_offsets, which calls _sibling_patches, which walks all of _entities' children -- and pests live there too. So the cost of drawing one patch scales with the number of pests, not the number of patches. _refresh_droplets queues a redraw whenever droplet_radius changes, which it does as pests enter and leave the patch, so the redraws are most frequent exactly when the pest count is highest. Sundew membership changes at only two sites, so the sibling list could be cached and invalidated there instead.
acceptance_criteria: Drawing a patch does not iterate pests. A test asserts the sibling lookup is not called per-pest, or that redraw cost is independent of pest count.

title: The 45-seed Corn upgrade is worse than the 20-seed one against a single pest
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS with evenly-spaced offsets puts level 3's kernels at +/-26, +/-13 and 0 degrees. Against Kernel.HIT_RADIUS 18.0 an outer kernel clears the aimed pest past 18/tan(26) = 37px -- under one cell, against a RANGE of 176. Level 2's +/-7 degrees connects out to 147px. Single-target that is level 2 at 2.78 dps versus level 3 at 1.61, and damage is 1.0 at all three levels. So the most expensive upgrade in the game makes a cob worse against the thing it is aimed at, while the selection panel advertises '5 kernel(s) per shot' and the muzzle fan draws the spread as the benefit.
acceptance_criteria: Each upgrade level is at least as good as the one below it against a single target, or the spread's cost is stated where the player buys it. A test asserts single-target dps is non-decreasing across levels.

title: The pause note is drawn underneath the first button
description: PauseScreen.FIRST_BUTTON_Y is an absolute 232.0 -- the one offset in that file not written as CARD.position.y + N. With CARD at y=152 the Note's box is 228-252 and ResumeButton's is 232-276, so 20 of the note's 24 pixels sit under an opaque stylebox. There is 64px of unused card below the last button. This is a sibling-pair overlap, the class validate-ui and findings structurally cannot see because each Control fits its own box; the repo ships .claude/skills/godot-hud-occlusion-audit for exactly this. The note text is also a constant, 'The wave is waiting.', which is false whenever pause fires between waves.
acceptance_criteria: No pause-screen Control overlaps another, asserted by a pairwise test, and the note says something true about the current state.

title: Two Sundews on the same ground cost 60 seeds and slow nothing extra
description: StickySundew refcounts its slow so overlapping patches hold a pest at 0.55 rather than 0.30 -- correct, and deliberate. But the patch wash composites darker where two patches overlap, so the only thing on screen says the opposite of the rule: it reads as 'more slow here'. A player can spend 60 seeds on two patches covering the same road and get exactly what one would have given. The placement preview has no notion of ground already covered, and crossing_time_multiplier() has no caller outside a test.
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping Sundew ground is visually distinguishable from stacked-and-working, or the preview warns before the second one is placed. A test covers the overlap case.

title: There is no pause, and no way to leave a run you are done with
description: get_tree().paused appears nowhere in game/. Game._unhandled_input handles motion, left click, KEY_R gated on game over, and KEY_M for mute -- there is no pause key. PREP_SECONDS keeps counting down while the player is away from the keyboard, so stepping away mid-run loses beds. TITLE_SCENE is reachable only from RunSummary's GateButton, which means the only way out of a run in progress is to lose it or kill the process. The devtools bridge answers while the tree is paused, so a pause menu is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: A pause key freezes the run including the prep timer, and offers a way back to the title screen. Unit test asserts the prep timer does not advance while paused.

title: Nothing in the catalogue answers a hungry pest
description: Sticky Sundew deliberately does not answer is_hungry: a hungry pest stops to eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0, under three seconds per bed, and eating is not movement-gated so a slow does nothing about it. Every plant in the catalogue either damages a pest or funds the ones that do; nothing protects or repairs a bed under attack. A real answer needs a regen or armour hook on Plant, which is why it was filed rather than faked.
acceptance_criteria: A plant, upgrade or mechanic exists that meaningfully changes the outcome when a hungry pest reaches a bed. Unit test drives a hungry pest against a defended and an undefended bed and asserts the difference.

title: A plant's health only goes down, and the cheapest repair is to destroy it
description: Plant.take_damage is the only writer of health and there is no heal path anywhere. uproot_refund reads PlantCatalog.cost * 0.6 and never reads health, so uprooting a nearly-dead plant refunds exactly as much as uprooting a pristine one -- making uproot-and-replant the cheapest repair in the game at a net 4 seeds for a Corn. That is a strictly dominant strategy that also makes the new health readout advisory rather than a decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either damaged plants can be healed at a cost, or the uproot refund scales with remaining health so a wrecked plant refunds less. Unit test covers the refund at full and near-zero health.

title: The placement ring is drawn with equal confidence over cells that cover no road at all
description: PlacementPreview computes reach and legality per cell but legality only means buildable-and-empty. Measured against the real PATH_CORNERS route: of 94 buildable cells, 15 cover zero road at a Corn Cobbler's RANGE of 176px, and 34 cover zero road at a Chomp Flower's GRAB_RADIUS of 73.6px. The ring looks identical on all of them, so a player can spend 10 seeds on a plant that can never fire, and nothing says so before or after the click.
acceptance_criteria: A cell that covers no road for the currently selected plant is visually distinct in the preview before the click. Unit test asserts the covered-road count per cell against the real route for both plants.

title: One high score serves both game modes, and the title screen names it wrong
description: Game._end_run calls RunConfig.record_score with the run's seed total and no mode check, and RunConfig persists a single number to user://highscore.save. TitleScreen renders that one number as 'Best endless run' / 'No endless run on record yet'. So a campaign run can take the endless record, and RunSummary._score_line then compares a campaign total against a number that may have come from an endless run. Two different games are sharing one scoreboard and the label claims otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign and endless keep separate high scores, each labelled for the mode it came from, and an existing single-value save migrates without being lost. Unit test covers a campaign run not overwriting an endless record.

title: The game makes no sound at all
description: A repo-wide grep for AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStream, .ogg and .wav finds no hit anywhere in game code -- assets/ holds only kenney/ and sprites/. Four new cues shipped in cycle 3-4 (uproot arming, plant damage, threat escalation, mutation markers) and not one of them makes a noise. The silent-death case is the worst: compost_meter erases an expired husk with no cue at all, so the player never learns they were too slow. Kenney ships CC0 audio packs in the same collection the sprites came from.
acceptance_criteria: At least placement, pest death, husk collection, husk rot and run end have distinct sounds, with a master mute honoured (devtools_config.json already sets mute:true for automation). A test asserts every declared sound file exists and loads.
close_reason: 11 CC0 Kenney samples, 8-voice root-parented pool, silent-husk-rot fixed; verified live catching a voice mid-playback and surviving a scene reload

title: A mutated pest is a tint, and the two that change the rules are unnamed
description: Pest mutations are signalled only by a _tint colour. Winged makes a Chomp Flower unable to grab it at all (chomp_flower.gd skips pests with is_winged) and hungry makes it eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0 -- under three seconds to destroy a bed. Both change what the player should do and neither is named or shaped differently. The placement preview already computes at_risk, so the vocabulary for warning about this exists.
acceptance_criteria: A winged and a hungry pest are each distinguishable from a plain one by something other than hue -- a shape, an icon, or a label -- and the distinction survives a screenshot in greyscale.

title: Nothing counts down the 18 seconds to the next wave
description: Game.PREP_SECONDS is 18.0 and _process silently decrements _prep_left until a wave starts on its own. The only mention is a 6-second message when the previous wave clears, so for the other 12 seconds the player has no idea how long they have to spend seeds and place plants. The threat tint now tells them how bad the next wave is and still nothing tells them when it lands.
acceptance_criteria: The HUD shows the remaining prep time and it visibly counts down; the readout disappears once a wave is live. Covered by a unit test that pumps _process and asserts the text changes.

title: The message line has one slot, so cues stomp each other
description: Hud.show_message assigns _message_label.text outright and resets a single _message_left timer, so any new message destroys the one before it mid-read. The uproot gate made this concrete: the 4s 'click again to uproot' instruction is wiped by the 2s husk message the moment a pest dies, and the player is left with an armed button and no explanation. A short queue, or a second line, or at minimum refusing to overwrite a higher-priority message before it has been readable.
acceptance_criteria: A message cannot be replaced before a minimum readable time unless the new one is higher priority; the uproot instruction survives an incidental husk pickup. Unit test drives two overlapping show_message calls and asserts what the label reads.

title: A real end-of-run summary panel
description: _end_run paints the run's whole damage map on the board and names the worst cell in a 30s message that expires while the player is still reading the banner. Every number a post-mortem needs is already computed -- waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned, high score, worst lane cell, husks collected vs dropped. Give them a panel that stays until dismissed, instead of a banner plus a timed message.
acceptance_criteria: An end-of-run panel showing at least waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned and the worst lane cell, which persists until the player restarts; covered by a headless UI test.
close_reason: RunSummary card with waves/threat/beds/compost/worst-cell, persists until dismissed, replay and back-to-title both wired and verified live

title: Show a selected plant's health in the side panel
description: Hungry pests chew plants down over several seconds and Plant.health drives a bar on the plant itself, but the selection panel shows only the name and blurb. Selecting a half-eaten Corn Cobbler tells the player nothing about whether to uproot and replant it, which is exactly the decision the panel exists to support. Add a health readout to the selection box.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel shows current/max health for a damaged plant and updates as it takes damage; a unit test drives take_damage and asserts the panel text changed.
close_reason: Health bar + numbers in the selection panel, hidden until damaged, green->red ramp; runtime caught a zero-margin panel foot which is now fixed and gated at 8px

title: Uproot needs a confirm or an undo
description: The Uproot button refunds 60% and destroys the plant instantly with no confirmation. One stray click on a selected Sunflower late in a run silently destroys the economy the whole run was built on -- it is the only irreversible misclick in the game. Add a confirm step (the button re-labels to 'Uproot? Confirm' for a few seconds) or a short undo window that restores the plant and reverses the refund.
acceptance_criteria: A single click on Uproot does not remove the plant; a second within the window does. Unit tests cover both the confirm path and the timeout-cancels path.
close_reason: request_uproot() arms on first click, commits on a second within 4s; verified live (232x40 relabel, exact UPROOT_ARMED red, timeout revert) and covered by 4 tests

title: Designer's Notebook reads as two floating images, not a notebook
description: Six pages, each a bare 320x320 drawing beside a bare 320x320 sprite on a flat dark field, with one six-word green caption and three default buttons below. Nothing says which pane is which, the sprite renders blurry (64px source filtered up to 320), there is no keyboard paging or Escape, no transition between pages, and the page/sprite mapping is wrong in places (image6 is the named Corn Cobbler portrait, not the kernel volley; image3 is where the kernels are).
acceptance_criteria: A paper spread with a binding so it reads as a notebook; per-pane headings; crisp sprite rendering; a real designer note per page, not just a caption; correct drawing-to-sprite mapping; page dots; Left/Right arrows page and Escape closes; a cross-fade between pages; Drawing/Sprite/PageLabel/Backdrop stay direct children of the root so existing tests and bridge paths hold.

title: Title screen is a flat rectangle with default-theme buttons
description: The title screen draws INK over the whole viewport, three stock grey Buttons and three Labels. No art, no motion, no keyboard, and the bottom third is empty — in a game that already ships plant and pest sprites. It is the first thing a player sees and it looks unfinished.
acceptance_criteria: A themed button set (paper/ink/leaf, hover + focus states); a drawn backdrop instead of one flat colour; the game's own sprites on screen; an entrance animation that is skipped headlessly; keyboard focus and Enter to start; existing node paths (Backdrop/StartButton/EndlessButton/NotebookButton) unchanged so tests and the bridge still resolve.

title: HUD compost counter collides with the Grow-the-next-wave button
description: With several husks on the ground the HUD reads 'Compost 0 (11 ready)' and the '(11 ready)' suffix runs underneath the 'Grow the next wave' button. Caught in a screenshot during /verify on 2026-08-15; validate-ui reported 0 findings over that exact frame because the label's own rect is fine -- it is the button that overlaps it, and nothing compares two sibling Controls for occlusion. Give the HUD bar a real layout (HBoxContainer with the button in its own slot) so the counter cannot be run over regardless of how long its text gets.
acceptance_criteria: A HUD with a 2-digit husk count and the wave button both visible has no overlapping screen rects, asserted by node-bounds in a test.

title: Mutated pests should drop a better husk
description: Armoured/winged/hungry mutations all cost the player more to deal with than a plain pest, but _on_pest_died pays the same husk value regardless of mutation. Scale husk value by mutation (e.g. armoured/winged/hungry each worth more) to tie the mutation system into the compost system instead of leaving them side by side.
close_reason: Pest.husk_multiplier() scales husk value by mutation (armoured/winged 1.5x, hungry 2x); verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (compost_state: plain=2, hungry=3)

title: Lane pressure readout on the road
description: The board is a single road, so which end pests got furthest on last wave is always answerable but never shown. Tint the road segment red where pests advanced furthest last wave, fading each wave, to give the player a passive read on lane pressure without opening any menu.
close_reason: LanePressureOverlay tints the road cell where pests got furthest last wave; verified headless (4 unit tests, one of which caught a real game-over-mid-wave commit bug) and live (board_info + run-method + screenshot)

title: Selection needs a second cue beyond the range ring
description: Right now the only sign a plant is selected is the translucent range ring — Corn Cobbler shows it, but Chomp Flower draws no ring at all, so selecting a Chomp shows nothing. Add a thin outline or corner brackets drawn on the sprite itself in the base Plant class (not per-subclass), so selection is legible for every current and future plant.
close_reason: SelectionMarker child node ships in Plant, verified headless (2 unit tests) and at runtime (get-state + screenshot)

title: Corn range indicator on selected plant
description: Placement is blind: corn reaches 176px and nothing shows it. Draw a range ring around the plant when selected/placing so the player can judge coverage.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Chomp Flower occupied readout
description: chew_progress() exists on ChompFlower and nothing draws it. The Chomp/beetle trade-off (mouth busy ~2.6s, lane open) is invisible to the player. Draw a shrinking ring/bar around the flower while chewing.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Sprite pass 2: damaged/eating/dead states
description: The design doc draws a Chomp mid-bite and an X-eyed pest; those are separate sprites, not tints.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Pest waves: aphid swarms and beetle heavies
description: Aphid = fast/weak, Beetle = slow/tanky and survives a Chomp long enough to matter.

title: Chomp Flower melee: instant on small pests, slow chew on big ones
description: 'eats small pests easily, takes a while eating bigger pests' — occupied-while-chewing is the whole balance lever.

title: Corn Cobbler firing: single kernel, then the 'bunch of corn' burst
description: Design doc shows a single projectile upgrading to a spread of kernels.

title: Seed economy: earn seeds, buy seed packets to unlock plants
description: 'You have to buy plant seeds to get plants' — seed drops from killed pests, a packet shop, and a run-persistent unlock set.

title: Plant placement and the one free starter plant
description: Corn Cobbler is free at wave 1 per the design doc; every other plant costs seeds.

title: Grid + path playfield from the Kenney tilesheet
description: Build the top-down lane using assets/kenney/png terrain tiles: dirt path over grass, buildable plots, spawn and base tiles.

title: The title column has no sixth slot at any price
description: BUTTON_TOP is 208, heights are 44/40 against a findings touch-target gate of 40, BUTTON_GAP is 8 - the Options row was paid for out of three places at once because no single one had slack. Five buttons now clear TitleBackdrop.HORIZON with nothing to spare. The next destination (credits, difficulty picker, trophy shelf if it leaves the notebook) has nowhere to go. Decide the shape now: scrolling list, two-column grid, or secondary destinations behind a single More door.

title: Reach the Options screen mid-run from the pause card
description: OptionsScreen (plant-tower-defense-lgv) lives on the title screen only, so a player who wants the colourblind bars on has to leave the run to find them -- which is the one moment they are most likely to want them. The pause card derives its own height from its contents (PauseScreen.card_rect) and cannot simply grow a button; see KeyBindingScreen's header for the same constraint. A sibling agent was concurrently making the Keys screen reachable from the pause card, so whatever shape that landed in is the shape this should follow.

title: The in-world plant health bar is a third red-lerp bar the colourblind option does not reach
description: plant-tower-defense-xu0 routed the HUD's two bars (Hud.health_color, Hud.threat_color) through RunConfig.colorblind_safe. Plant.HEALTH_BAR_HURT / the ColorRect Plant draws over itself on the board is a third bar on the same green-to-red ramp, and it is the one a player actually watches during a chew - the HUD's copy only appears for the selected plant. Found live: one find-nodes --class ColorRect sweep showed Entities/*/ColorRect at LEAF (0.18, 0.8, 0.443) beside a HUD fill on the safe ramp. HEALTH_BAR_HURT is also still a hand-typed copy of GardenTheme.DANGER, which garden_theme.gd's own doc comment already flags; folding it in and routing it through Hud.health_color_on would fix both at once.

title: A colorblind-safe palette swap for the two red-lerp health/threat bars
description: A plant's health bar (HEALTH_LOW.lerp(HEALTH_FULL, fraction)) and the wave threat_color() both ease through the same red-family ramp by hue alone. Consider a colorblind-safe palette swap (blue-orange) as an alternative or companion to the existing accessibility commitment (distinct pest shapes) - the two combat bars a player watches hardest are still hue-only cues. (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 18/'meta systems' batch.)
close_reason: Shipped in 0480e2d. GardenTheme gains SAFE_GOOD/SAFE_MID/SAFE_BAD (blue through light orange to bright orange); Hud.threat_color and a new Hud.health_color now delegate to pure threat_color_on(level, safe)/health_color_on(fraction, safe), so both bars go through one switch and the ramp selection is assertable as data. The flag is RunConfig.colorblind_safe, persisted (SAVE_VERSION 4 adds a 'cb0'/'cb1' options line; a v3 file migrates forward with it off), toggled by C in-run with a KEY_HELP row - a placeholder for a settings screen, which does not exist in this worktree. 10 new tests plus the existing threat-ramp test re-pointed at threat_color_on(level, false) so it no longer depends on a process-global option. The measurement test caught the first stops being WORSE than the ramp they replace (0.157 of luminance between the ends against green/red's 0.267); the shipped stops measure 0.36.

title: No milestones/achievements - RunSummary's totals die with the scene
description: RunSummary.summary_rows() totals waves survived, pests killed, threat reached and more from data Game has been accumulating the whole run; RunConfig._save() writes exactly three lines (version header + two high scores), throwing every other total away the instant the title screen loads. A small persisted set of milestone flags, checked once at _end_run against numbers the game is already holding, is most of an achievements system without a single new gameplay counter. (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 11.)
close_reason: Shipped in 7e9dafa. game/milestones.gd holds a seven-entry table (campaign_cleared, unbroken_garden, hundred_pests, five_hundred_pests, endless_deep, threat_peak, clean_sweep) evaluated as pure static code against the stats Dictionary Game.summary_stats already builds - no new gameplay counters. RunConfig's save shape goes to v3 with a fourth 'm<count>:<ids>' line (count-prefixed so a truncated line is refused rather than read as an empty set); a v2 file migrates forward with an empty set. Game._end_run files them and RunConfig.record_milestones returns only the newly-earned ones, which the results card lists in a MilestoneRibbon beside it. 13 new tests: the evaluation table at and one under every threshold, the persistence round trip, the v2 migration, eight malformed-milestone-line refusals, and the ribbon's geometry.

title: No InputMap - four (now five) keys are raw scancode checks with no settings screen
description: project.godot has no [input] section. Every binding is a raw scancode compared inline: KEY_R (game_over/victory), KEY_ESCAPE/KEY_P (pause), KEY_M (sfx mute), KEY_N (music mute, added this session), plus NotebookScreen's own three keys. Game.KEY_HELP is the one place these are named, rendered only as a legend on the pause card - nothing calls InputMap.add_action. A settings screen that reads/writes these bindings through a real InputMap, persisted beside RunConfig's scores, turns the printed legend into a configurable one. (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 11.)
close_reason: Shipped in two commits on worktree-agent-a8622dffea8874c70. (1) e6a17a1 migrates all seven keyboard verbs to a runtime-registered InputMap (KeyBindings.ACTIONS is the single source of defaults + descriptions), replaces every inline keycode==KEY_* check with event.is_action_pressed, derives Game.key_help() (was const KEY_HELP) from the InputMap so the pause card's legend follows a rebinding, and extends RunConfig's save to v3 with a count-prefixed block holding only the rows that differ from the defaults. (2) 3cf1863 adds KeyBindingScreen, reachable from a new Keys button on the title screen: one row per verb, Change arms a row, the next key lands on it, a clash is refused with a reason, Escape backs out, 'Put them all back' resets, every change persisted through RunConfig.store_key_bindings. 448 unit tests pass (up from 437); verified live over the bridge - input list shows the actions, input tap opens/closes the pause card, and a rebind through the screen moved garden_restart to F5 on disk. Found while verifying: the migrated handlers still narrowed to InputEventKey, so Input.action_press could not reach any verb - fixed and covered.

title: Starting a wave has no sound of its own
description: Hud._next_wave_button.pressed (hud.gd:486) just emits next_wave_requested with no Sfx.play() call; Sfx.WAVE_STARTED only plays later once _on_wave_started actually fires. The deliberate click that starts the countdown is the one press in the whole attack chain (plant sounds, kernel hit flash, wave-clear banner) with no feedback of its own. Add a distinct button-press cue to the Grow-the-next-wave button.
close_reason: Shipped in 5e6f766: new Sfx.BUTTON_PRESSED (minimize_006.ogg at -10 dB, the quietest row in the table) plays from Game._on_next_wave_requested, a handler now sitting between hud.next_wave_requested and start_next_wave so the prep-timer expiry and the devtools start_wave verb stay silent. Extended to the plant bar (_on_plant_chosen), the other press with no cue of its own; Upgrade, Uproot and the packets were deliberately left alone since each already rings its own outcome and PURCHASE_DENIED stays the only sound a refused press makes. Note the issue's premise about timing: WAVE_STARTED is NOT later - start_next_wave reaches wave_started synchronously, so the bell is in the press's own frame, which is why the press cue is trimmed to sit under it. Verified live: Voice0 minimize_006 at -10.0, Voice1 impactBell at 0.0, same press, wave 1 live.

title: Three warning colours on the board are the same red at different alphas
description: LanePressureOverlay's tint, a plant's health bar, and an armed Uproot all resolve through GardenTheme.DANGER at different alphas - three different sentences (pests got this far / this plant is dying / you are about to destroy this) in one hue. Worth a second channel - a shape, a hatch pattern, a tick mark - so the three don't rely on alpha alone to stay distinguishable, which also happens to be the accessibility-safe fix (colour alone is not colourblind-safe). (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 12.)
close_reason: Already shipped in commit 066cfe3 (A solid red warns, a broken red records), an ancestor of this branch's HEAD. That commit examined exactly these three sites and found two of the three named pairings were never actually confusable: lane pressure and the plant health bar never share a cell (plants only stand on buildable ground, roads never are), and the armed Uproot cue is a HUD Button font_color override, not a board surface, already carrying two non-colour channels (relabelled text + Sfx.UPROOT_ARMED). The pair that did collide -- Game._update_cursor's blocked-cell hover wash stacked on LanePressureOverlay's tint, both flat GardenTheme.DANGER squares on the same road cells during prep -- got the actual fix: lane pressure is now a 45-degree hatch (LanePressureOverlay.HATCH_SPACING/is_hatched()), tested in test_board.gd and test_combat.gd. The same commit also gave the health bar a colour-blind-safe fix (solid while bleeding, notched into HEALTH_BAR_SEGMENTS while regrowing), tested via Plant.health_bar_color(). Verified: name_check.py clean, lint_project.gd 0 errors/0 warnings, run_tests.gd 432/432 passing (9315 assertions). Updated kanban.md's cycle-12 backlog entry (still unmarked, which is why this got re-filed) to point at the fix so it isn't filed a third time.

title: A swept husk's seeds appear on the HUD with no visual connection to where it was collected
description: CompostMeter.collect_at() erases the husk from _husks the instant it is clicked, HuskLayer stops drawing it since it only iterates compost.husks(), and Game._click_at hands the value straight to bank.add_seeds(swept) - which lands in the Seeds stat at the top of the HUD, well away from the click. Only a queued caption connects the two events. A seed glyph that flies from the husk's own position to the Seeds label, sized off HuskLayer.radius_for(value), would carry the payout across the screen instead of asking the player to read the same number twice in two different places. (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 20.)
close_reason: Shipped in commit e85fa6b (Fly a seed glyph from a swept husk to the Seeds label). CompostMeter.husk_collected now carries the husk's board position; a new SeedGlyph Control, sized off HuskLayer.radius_for(value), tweens from there to the Seeds label under a new Hud._fx_layer and shrinks as it flies, then frees itself -- purely cosmetic, gated off entirely (no node created) under GardenTheme.animations_enabled() == false. Board-to-screen conversion is one _entities.to_global(at) call, the same 72px CanvasLayer offset corn_cobbler.gd's kernel-seeding comment names. _fx_layer is a Container rather than a plain Control specifically to satisfy two checks that disagreed: full-rect read as an overlap to test_selftest.gd's _hud_rects and to a person; zero-size passed that but tripped devtools findings' ui_zero_size. Verified: name_check.py, world_control_check.py and suite_reach_check.py clean; lint_project.gd 0 errors/0 warnings; run_tests.gd 435/435 passing (3 new tests: launch() sizing off HuskLayer.radius_for, total no-op headless leaving _fx_layer empty, and the real CompostMeter->Game->Hud signal chain end to end); live bridge verification at reduced game speed showed the glyph open at the husk's exact drop position and radius and begin flying toward the Seeds label (screenshots), with devtools findings 0/5 checks both before and after including the slow scene pass.

title: Music has exactly one volume: on or off
description: Music.BASE_VOLUME_DB (music.gd:53) is a fixed constant; the only control anywhere is Sfx.set_muted()/KEY_M, which silences both SFX and music together. No independent music/SFX balance. At minimum, split Music onto its own mute/volume state distinct from Sfx's, reachable from the pause card - a full settings screen with sliders is the larger version of this, filed separately if wanted.
close_reason: Music has its own is_muted/set_muted/toggle_muted, independent of Sfx's; reachable via a new KEY_N binding listed on the pause card. No persistence added, matching Sfx's own (unsaved) mute. Commit 5449122.

title: StickySundew's _wash_order counter never resets
description: StickySundew._next_wash_order (sticky_sundew.gd:112) is a class-level static that only ever goes up - not on reload_current_scene, not between runs. Nothing breaks at any plausible count, but it is a number that only increases for as long as the process lives, in a file that also keeps a static list of live patches (_live). Worth a deliberate decision: either document why it is safe to never reset (and add a test pinning that a very large value still orders correctly), or reset it at a defined point (e.g. when the last patch is freed, or on a fresh run start).
close_reason: Chose (a) reset: _exit_tree resets _next_wash_order to 0 the instant _live empties -- the one moment resetting costs nothing, since nothing alive could still be compared against the number being handed back. Pinned by a new test (constructs+frees a warmup patch to prove the counter was >0, then confirms it drops to exactly 0 once the only live patch is freed). Verified headless (name_check, lint, run_tests 421/421, meta_key/group_leak/suite_reach/settle_read checkers all clean of new findings) and live: placed a Sundew (wash_order=1), freed it through its own exit tween, placed a second at a fresh cell, and confirmed it also got wash_order=1 rather than 2.

title: Notebook page dots snap while the page turns with a tween
description: NotebookPage.current_page's setter (notebook_page.gd:38-41) calls queue_redraw() and nothing else, so the filled dot jumps to the new page the instant _page changes (notebook_screen.gd:547) - in the same frame _play_turn() (notebook_screen.gd:577) is still partway through its fade. Ease the dot transition (a small tween on its fill/position) so it turns alongside the page rather than ahead of it.
close_reason: NotebookPage's dot now eases via a tweened _display_page in step with the page-turn fade instead of snapping ahead of it. Commit 0f801aa.

title: No music system exists, only one-shot SFX
description: Sfx.SOUNDS (sfx.gd:68+) is entirely footsteps, impacts and stingers - every entry plays once and stops. No AudioStreamPlayer anywhere drives a loop; no title theme, no bed under a wave. A bigger feature ask than the other juice items: stand up a looping music system (title theme + in-run bed, at minimum), respecting the existing mute toggle (Sfx.set_muted / KEY_M).
close_reason: Shipped: MusicPlayer (game/music.gd) with two real CC0 Kenney loops (Farm Frolics = title/results, Mission Plausible = in-run), crossfaded on scene transitions, gated on Sfx's mute. Tests in test_selftest.gd; verified live via devtools bridge across title->game->results->replay->gate.

title: The title screen has zero motion anywhere
description: TitleBackdrop (title_backdrop.gd) draws sky, glow, ground, a scalloped grass edge and tufts across six _draw_* functions, all static geometry - no Tween, no per-frame value anywhere in the file. It is the first thing every player sees, and now the one screen in the game with no motion at all, contrasted against plants swaying idly, selection brackets growing in, HUD readouts punching, and cards rising/falling elsewhere. Add ambient motion - drifting clouds, swaying grass tufts, or similar - gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled().
close_reason: Added ambient motion to TitleBackdrop: drifting clouds, tuft sway, glow pulse, all gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(). Commit 8ffb986.

title: The prep bar has no final-second urgency
description: Hud._refresh_prep_bar (hud.gd:671-682) shrinks _prep_bar in lockstep with prep_left and tints it by next_threat_level - real information, calmly delivered, with the same steady shrink for all eighteen seconds. The last second or two before a wave lands is exactly when a player most wants a nudge. Add a brief pulse on _prep_bar.modulate once prep_left drops under ~2 seconds, reusing the same _ease_threat_tint-style kill-and-restart Tween shape t5l already applied to the HUD readout punches.
close_reason: Prep bar pulses (modulate alpha, looping kill-and-restart tween) once prep_left crosses PREP_BAR_URGENT_SECONDS=2.0; edge-detected so refresh()'s per-frame calls don't restart it. Verified live via bridge with a slowed game-speed window. Commit 676c465.

title: A seed packet's gamble resolves in the same frame it is bought
description:
SeedBank's own header calls a packet purchase "a gamble rather than a menu" and "with
a short catalogue that reads as suspense" (seed_bank.gd:8-10), but buy_packet()
(seed_bank.gd:176-197) deducts the cost, rolls the pool and emits plant_unlocked in
one synchronous call, landing as a text banner the instant the button is released. No
beat between spending the seeds and knowing the result. Add a brief reveal -- even a
short flicker through the tier-eligible pool before landing on the roll -- so the
suspense the code's own comment promises actually shows up on screen.
close_reason: Added Game._open_packet(): a short 3-step, ~0.27s flourish flashing other tier-eligible candidates before Game._reveal_plant_unlock shows the real banner (now MESSAGE_IMPORTANT so it isn't queued behind an ambient hint). buy_packet() itself is untouched/synchronous. Gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); headless keeps the instant reveal. Commit cf352da.

title: Distinguish naming a symbol from checking it
description: suite_reach_check concedes 'naming is a floor, not exercise' - a test writing WaveDirector.reset() and asserting nothing counts as reach. The honest upgrade is not a stricter name match but a second signal: whether the named symbol appears inside an assert_* argument or only in a statement. That distinguishes 'called it' from 'checked it' without pretending to understand the test.
close_reason: Added assert-argument co-occurrence as a second, advisory-only signal in suite_reach_check.py (commit 489193e). Naming still gates exactly as before; the new NOTE reports how many reached gating symbols never sit inside a _T.assert_*(...) argument anywhere in the test tree. Docstring extended (new WHAT THE ASSERT SIGNAL section + NOT COVERED caveat). Checker sanity-run clean against the repo (283 reached, 85 assert-only-absent). Headless /verify gates (name_check, import_check, lint, run_tests) all clean; full runtime bridge skipped as this touches no .gd/.tscn.

title: Measure how far coverage over-promises
description: The derived coverage map is an upper bound: a Corn shoots only the furthest-along pest, a busy Chomp grabs nothing, a winged pest is unreachable by a Chomp. So 'covered' over-promises exactly when a player is losing. An observed map was rejected because _ever_engaged is monotone - but a per-cell record of 'something was in range and did not fire' is not monotone and would measure the over-promise directly.

title: Let a plant declare whether it engages, instead of a list two files away
description: Game.ENGAGING_PLANTS is a positive list of CORN and CHOMP. A fifth plant fails a test, which is the right failure, but it fails AFTER someone has written the plant. A PlantCatalog entry could declare it, so the answer lives with the plant. Note PlantCatalog.reach() is NOT this - it returns SAP_RADIUS for the Sundew for the dead-ground cue, and a Sundew engages nothing.

title: Map where the garden never reached, not just that it did not
description: was_engaged() answers one question at one instant, at the exit. The same flag sampled per road cell would say WHERE the garden stopped reaching - the coverage-hole map the post-mortem's 'walked in untouched' line currently only aggregates. Genuinely different from lane pressure: pressure says where they got to, this says where nothing could touch them.

title: cmd budgets refuses to answer without a Game in the tree
description: The budgets verb returns 'no Game in the tree' on the title screen. Two of its six entries do not need a Game at all: notebook_subhead builds its own SubViewport, and road_shape reads Board statics. The notebook budget in particular is about a title-screen subscreen, so requiring a run to read it is backwards. Degrade per entry instead of refusing wholesale.
close_reason: Shipped: road_shape builds a throwaway Board, 4 remaining entries degrade to unmeasured per-entry, commit 96acf81

title: Nothing stops the sixth world-space Control forgetting the rule
description: Plant and Pest each grew a _make_world_controls_click_through(), deliberately duplicated rather than shared. Two copies of a rule with no third enforcement. The test enumerates the live tree so it would catch a new offender, but only one on screen during that test - a Control appearing only on a boss wave, or in a menu the test never opens, is invisible to it.

title: An escape records nothing about how it happened
description: _on_pest_escaped files every escape against Board.exit_cell() because the pest's own position is off-board when the signal fires. Eight beetles through one gap and eight stragglers over forty waves produce byte-identical evidence. The pest knows where it entered the exit cell from, how long it survived, and what it walked past untouched.

title: BLOCKED_COLOR is a hand-typed near-red the palette merge missed
description: PlacementPreview.BLOCKED_COLOR is Color(0.95, 0.42, 0.36, 0.75), a hand-typed near-red that the GardenTheme palette merge did not catch. It should probably alias GardenTheme.DANGER. Note it draws brackets (already a shape channel) rather than a surface, so it is a value change belonging to the merge, not a legibility fix.

title: Separate what is true of a road from what is true of THIS road
description: PATH_CORNERS produces 32 road cells and 2112px of walking. At least four things are calibrated against that route: the endless road budget's pests-per-cell, the Sundew's coverage arithmetic, the dead-ground count of 15 of 94, and the husk clearance. Each is tested individually; a second route would move all four at once and nothing says which are properties of a road and which of this one.

title: The title screen's lawn and the notebook both predate half the catalogue
